$comment: Model-name rewrites applied to vendored upstream files, in order. Each rule is a literal find/replace scoped to upstream paths by glob. `count` is the exact number of replacements the rule must make across its files; a mismatch fails the sync so upstream changes are never rewritten blindly. Team models: each member runs Claude Code (Opus 5.5, max effort). So every judgment, prose, and panel role is `inherit-parent`: it runs on the member's own agent, and panels get their independent opinions from separate runs. Code delegates are the exception the owner chose: they run on `sonnet` (Claude Sonnet 5.5), or `haiku` (Claude Haiku 5.5) for trivial mechanical edits. An explicit model name survives only as an example a user can type, and a GPT name is always `gpt-6-sol-high`.

rules.from: Families go by prefix, and the longest match wins: `claude-fable-*`, `claude-*`, and `gemini-*`, after dropping a leading `cursor-`.
rules.to: Families go by prefix, and the longest match wins: `claude-*` and `gpt-*`.

rules.from: So `medium` turns `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh-fast` into `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` and `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` into `claude-opus-5-5-medium-fast`, and `small` turns them into `claude-opus-5-5-medium-fast` and `claude-opus-5-5-low-fast`. Opus 5.5 always runs its `-fast` slug, so every Opus 5.5 value ends in `-fast`. Fable 5.2 and Gemini have no fast slug, so never write one. Gemini 4 Neon slugs run from `low` to `xhigh` with no `max` or `fast` slug, so its seat runs at `gemini-4-neon-xhigh`, its top slug. A Gemini 4 Neon entry in a panel role takes its own target, `xhigh` moved by the budget, so `large` keeps `gemini-4-neon-xhigh`, `medium` writes `gemini-4-neon-high`, and `small` writes `gemini-4-neon-medium`.

rules.to: - Code, including the hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms): `sonnet` (Claude Sonnet 5.5). Prose and judgment: `inherit-parent`. The Task tool takes these aliases, not version slugs.
- Trivial mechanical edits (a rename, a move, a formatting or one-line fix, or steps specified to the letter with nothing to decide): `haiku` (Claude Haiku 5.5), the `trivial edits` line.

rules.from: The hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) go to your `hardest tasks` model (default `claude-fable-5-2-max`), whether the task needs judgment on vague intent or is a precisely specified sequence of steps to execute to the letter. Trivial mechanical edits go to your `swarm workers` model (default `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`). Review and design panels default to one runner each on `claude-fable-5-2-high`, `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`, and `gemini-4-carbon-high`.
rules.to: A feature, refactor, bug fix, perf fix, hillclimb step, or one of the hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) goes to `sonnet` (Claude Sonnet 5.5). A trivial mechanical edit (a rename, a move, a formatting or one-line fix, or steps specified to the letter with nothing to decide) goes to `haiku` (Claude Haiku 5.5), the `trivial edits` line. The Task tool takes these aliases, not version slugs. Review and design panels default to one runner each on `inherit-parent`, `inherit-parent`, and `inherit-parent`.

rules.from: **Fable 5.2 is an exception.** It runs outside a panel only when the user named it for this task or two Opus 5.5 xhigh runs of the same brief failed its check. Say which. Difficulty alone never qualifies.
A Gemini seat runs at `gemini-4-neon-xhigh` unless its line names another level.

Older defaults put another Gemini model, then `gemini-4-neon-high`, in the panel seat. So in any rule, a `gemini-4-neon-high` entry, or a `gemini-4-*` entry other than `gemini-4-neon-*`, in a panel role (`arena runners`, `arena cross-judge pool`, `interrogate reviewers`) is an old default. Each one becomes `gemini-4-neon-xhigh`. A Gemini 4 Neon entry at any other level is the user's choice and stays. Tell the user which entries you replaced.

- An `arena cross-judge pool` list of exactly one `claude-fable-*` entry, one `claude-opus-*` entry, and one `gemini-*` entry, in any order, takes the role's step 5 list. Fable and Opus are one vendor, so the Fable entry could judge only where the Opus entry also could.

code delegates (feature, refactoring, bug fix, perf, hillclimb), prose, and judgment go to opus 5.5 at xhigh, and no role runs above xhigh. outside a review panel, fable 5.2 runs only when you name it or after two opus 5.5 runs of the same brief fail. the default panel is fable 5.2 / opus 5.5 / gemini 4 neon.
